sections.html:
South Jordan occupies the middle of the Salt Lake Valley, roughly 18 miles south of the capital, and slopes from the Jordan River up toward the Oquirrh foothills. Residents numbered 77,487 in 2020, compared with 50,418 ten years before. Fast growth like that leaves a lot of fairly new houses, so questions about roof age and basement permits are routine.

Housing measureSouth Jordan, 2020 to 2024
Owner-occupied housing rate81.4%
Median value of owner-occupied homes$650,500
Median gross rent$1,991
Persons per household3.09
Median household income$134,047

Treat the median as a survey figure and not a quote for your address. A house with a worn roof, an unfinished basement or a dated kitchen sells under it, and a lakeview Daybreak home can sell over it.

Because the whole city falls inside one county, all three property offices belong to Salt Lake County. Jordan School District runs the public schools, including Bingham High and Herriman High.

sections.h2: Daybreak and the construction around it
sections.html:
Daybreak is a master-planned community of about 4,200 acres on the west side, started in 2004 by Kennecott Land. The remaining 1,300 undeveloped acres were sold to Larry H. Miller Group in 2022, and a new Downtown Daybreak opened in 2025 with the Salt Lake Bees ballpark as its anchor.

The city describes Downtown Daybreak as part of a Housing Transit Reinvestment Zone along the Mountain View Corridor, between two existing TRAX stations. If you live on the west side, plan for more building nearby for several more years, and be upfront about noise, traffic and showing schedules.

Commute questions come first from out-of-town buyers. Freeway I-15 skirts the east side, exiting at 10600 South and 11400 South, and Bangerter Highway cuts through the center with ramps at 9800, 10400 and 11400 South.

  • TRAX Red Line: three Daybreak stations, at South Jordan Parkway, South Jordan Downtown and Daybreak Parkway. The ride from Daybreak Parkway to downtown Salt Lake City takes about 60 minutes.
  • FrontRunner commuter rail: a station at 10200 South.
  • Charter and private options: Paradigm High, Early Light Academy, Hawthorne Academy, American Heritage and Stillwater Academy.

What is allowed hinges on the kind of property. Condos, townhouses, single-family houses and guest houses may host nightly stays, though a guest house first needs an approved accessory dwelling unit permit. A basement apartment is an internal ADU and cannot be rented nightly.

Did you ever advertise your finished basement online? A lender or inspector may raise it, and the space could only qualify as a long-term rental.

City code 5.04.100 makes business licenses non-transferable, and applications go through the city's online portal. Your license will not pass to the buyer, so be careful how you describe rental income.

Inspectors raise both, and both are ordinary for homes in this part of Utah. The Wasatch Fault is roughly 240 miles long, and the odds of a magnitude 6.0 or stronger earthquake inside 50 years are estimated at 57%. In March 2020 a 5.7 quake near Magna damaged buildings across the valley.

Radon is a gas that seeps up from the ground. The state radon program reports elevated readings in one of every three Utah homes and sets the action level at 4 picocuries per liter. Testing is advised, and a result above that level may mean installing a mitigation system.

With a cash purchase as is, both just become part of the price conversation.

The county sends the bill, and November 30 is the cutoff for paying this year's tax with no penalty. On December 1, any unpaid real property tax is delinquent.

  • Valuation notices go out by July 22.
  • Tax notices are mailed by November 1.
  • Late payers owe the greater of 2.5% or $10, which shrinks to 1% when the balance is cleared by January 31.

A primary residence is 45% exempt, which leaves 55% of market value as the taxable amount. The Treasurer's office is at 2001 S State St, Suite N1-200, Salt Lake City, phone (385) 468-8300. The Recorder, who files your deed, is in Suite N1-600 at (385) 468-8145.

Appeals to the Board of Equalization are open from August 1 to September 15. Think your valuation is high? Collect nearby sales, repair quotes and photos of trouble spots such as an aging roof or a damaged basement before the window opens. A well-organized file is your best argument.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in South Jordan
sections.html:
Selling for cash removes the loan, so nothing depends on a bank's appraisal or approval. Ask for an offer, let the buyer look over the property, and then name a closing date that suits your schedule.

A title or escrow company still handles the closing, and the Salt Lake County Recorder files the deed. Tax is split by days owned, so your share at closing follows how much of the year the house was yours. Expect questions about the roof, heating and cooling system and any finished basement, and dig up those records before you request offers.

Overdue taxes or a lien on the title are paid off from your proceeds when the sale closes, and the title company lists each amount for you.

sections.h2: What to gather before you sell
sections.html:
A little preparation shortens any sale. Pull your most recent property tax notice, the mortgage payoff amount if there is a loan, and any paperwork for work done on the house. If a basement or garage was finished, locate the permit. If a unit was rented, find the lease and note the deposit.

Also decide what stays. Appliances, window coverings and the garage door openers are all fair questions on closing day, and settling them early prevents last-minute friction.

Finally, talk to your lender or the title company about timing. If you have already bought another house, tell the buyer, because a flexible closing date, either soon or later, is often worth more to a stressed seller than a slightly higher price.

• Basement or garage conversions built without a permit, which the city will not count as legal units.
  • A short-term rental history that conflicts with the rules for the property type.
  • Daybreak construction that changes noise, traffic and showing schedules.
  • High radon results that appear late in a financed sale.
  • A tight timeline because you have already bought another house.

Learn about any of these before the first showing, not after an offer. If one applies to you, say so when you ask for a cash offer so the number you receive already accounts for it.

faqs.q: Is South Jordan in Salt Lake County?
faqs.a: Yes, all of it. Three county offices (Assessor, Treasurer and Recorder) deal with valuation, tax and deed, and the city's schools belong to Jordan School District.

faqs.q: When are South Jordan property taxes due?
faqs.a: Pay by November 30 to avoid a penalty. After that the tax is delinquent, though a balance cleared by January 31 only carries the 1% rate.

faqs.q: Can I use a basement apartment in South Jordan as an Airbnb?
faqs.a: No, a basement apartment is an internal ADU and the city bars it from nightly rental. Other property types, including a permitted guest house, can qualify under the license rules.

faqs.q: How many people live in South Jordan?
faqs.a: About 77,487 in the 2020 count, up from 50,418 in 2010.

faqs.q: Can I sell a South Jordan house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer accepts the house as is and factors in the work. Request the offer in writing and weigh it against what you would keep after fixing and listing.
